facts.text: I've been having trouble walking up stairs.
My muscles get stronger once I've been active for a while, and climbing stairs gets easier.

facts.item: how long the symptoms have been going on
facts.text: I've had the cough and the trouble with stairs for 3 months.
I've lost a significant amount of weight: 4.6 kg over the past 6 months.
I've smoked a pack of cigarettes a day for 35 years.
I live in a two-story apartment without an elevator.

leakage.reason: The antibody result names the diagnosis ('supportive of Lambert-Eaton syndrome diagnosis'). Kept per CONVERSION.md (a result may state what the test shows); it is only seen when the doctor orders this specific antibody test.

source_issues: The gold diagnosis is visible in the VGCC antibody result (pool flags: visible_gold_alias_partitions test_results, requires_diagnosis_text_cleanup true).
ROS (p007) lists 'slow pupil reaction', an examination sign, under neurological symptoms.
Smoking history is recorded under Past_Medical_History.
The weight loss is over 6 months, longer than the 3-month history of cough and stair difficulty (not a contradiction).
notes: 'Slow pupil reaction' (ROS) is observer-only and already in the pupillary-reflex exam leaf (x007), so no patient fact was created for it.
Improvement with activity appears in p001 (stairs), p004 and p007 (muscle weakness/strength); it applies to both the stair difficulty and the weakness, so it is one standalone fact (f004).
The 3-month duration covers both the cough and the stair difficulty (standalone f005); the 6-month period belongs to the weight loss (f007).
Dry mucous membranes are only an examination finding; no dry-mouth complaint is in the patient fragments, so none was created.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with cough, difficulty walking up stairs, and muscle strength changes.
